chunks: I looked around but found no one to shield me, protect me or help me except the members of my family. I refrained from flinging them into death and therefore closed my eyes despite the dust, kept swallowing saliva despite (the suffocation of) grief and endured pangs of anger although it was more bitter than colocynth and more grievous than the bite of knives.

key_terms.الْقَذى: Dust or grit (metaphor for minor annoyances or grief)
key_terms.ذَابٌّ: One who removes obstacles or defends

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali demonstrate patience and reliance on his family during times of hardship?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in the context of the 'Period of Silence' (Dawr al-Samt) or the lead-up to the Battle of Siffin, underscores the strategic patience of Imam Ali (AS) as he endured the political marginalization by the Quraysh elite. By prioritizing the preservation of his family and the broader Muslim community over immediate personal vengeance, he exemplifies the Shia virtue of *kathm al-ghayz* (concealing anger) as a means of maintaining political stability and spiritual integrity.
